hypotheses.statement: Inspect the deployed launch flags, checkout, patch, and container first: the supplied profile says DSpark k5 has adaptive verification disabled, while its CSV says DSpark is off. If verification is inactive and the DeepSeek-specific graph safety conditions are present or can be qualified, enable adaptive verification while retaining draft k5. The proposed mechanism is to spend less target verification work when a full drafted block is unlikely to be useful. This is a transfer inference, not an observed B200 benefit. The B300 concurrent-prefill failure makes mixed-batch graph eligibility a prerequisite, and the B200 tuning PR favors fixed k5. Advance only if same-topology tests improve SLO-qualified cost and throughput without sampling, rollback, or latency regressions.
hypotheses.observed_bottleneck: Unknown on the target deployment. No supplied result isolates verification cost on 8×B200.
hypotheses.mechanism: Adaptive verification may reduce target work while keeping the draft width at k5; mixed prefill must avoid unsafe FULL graph capture.
hypotheses.proposed_change: After flag and code inspection, qualify graph-safe mixed prefill and decode, then toggle enable_adaptive_verification with draft k5 fixed. Keep any safety patch separate from the toggle.
hypotheses.code_surface: Deployed launch configuration; DSpark adaptive verification; DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse attention metadata builders and CUDA graph eligibility.
hypotheses.applicability: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8×B200, 2×DEP4 baseline, agent-f75 and fixed Mooncake traces. Transfer from B300 and GLM is unproven.
hypotheses.predicted_direction: Possible increase in SLO-qualified goodput per GPU dollar and decrease in cost per successful million output tokens; size and even sign are unknown.

hypotheses.statement: Consider verification-cost calibration only if deployed inspection shows adaptive verification is eligible, graph safety is qualified, and its cost model uses profiling shapes above the reachable decode ceiling. A B200 issue reports that such shapes can be mistaken for uniform decode; an open PR proposes schedulable mixed prefill and decode tails. Port or enable that behavior only if absent from the frozen runtime, and retain the current captured decode shapes. The mechanism is a more faithful cost estimate for the batches that actually occur, which might change adaptive decisions under prefill pressure. No supplied evidence shows that calibration improves serving performance on this target; if the behavior already exists or decisions do not change, stop.
hypotheses.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The supplied B200 issue identifies an invalid profiling shape, not a measured target serving bottleneck.
hypotheses.mechanism: Scheduler-reachable mixed-batch profiling could correct verification-cost estimates used by an eligible adaptive policy.
hypotheses.proposed_change: Inspect whether #54077 or equivalent behavior is present. If absent and relevant, use explicit mixed decode/prefill tail splits above the k5 decode ceiling, preserving captured graph shapes; isolate this change from graph safety and adaptive activation.
hypotheses.code_surface: AdaptiveVerificationManager batches_to_profile, dummy-run scheduling and context, model runner profiling, and cost selection.
hypotheses.applicability: Conditional on an active adaptive policy and a reachable tail-shape mismatch in the frozen B200 runtime. Effect on target workload is unknown.
hypotheses.predicted_direction: Potentially better policy decisions and SLO-qualified cost-throughput; no directional benefit is established without decision and cost traces.
